News Flash

Boca Raton Explores the Future of Mobility at its 2nd Annual Mobility Workshop

Media Releases Posted on October 15, 2026

The City of Boca Raton will host its 2nd Annual Mobility Workshop on Thursday, October 29, from 4:30 to 7:00 pm at Florida Atlantic University (FAU), bringing residents and community members together to learn about current mobility projects and explore ideas shaping the future of transportation.

Hosted at Gangal Hall at FAU’s Engineering East building, the free workshop is presented in partnership with the FAU College of Engineering & Computer Science and the FAU Chapter of the Institute of Transportation Engineers.

The workshop will provide an opportunity for residents and visitors to connect with local transportation agencies and partners, hear updates on mobility efforts in Boca Raton, and discover innovative ideas from FAU students.

Participating organizations will include the Palm Beach Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO), Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT), Circuit, and the City of Boca Raton’s Fire Rescue Services Department and Office of Sustainability, giving attendees an opportunity to learn more about the work and resources available across the region.

EVENT DETAILS

WHAT: 2nd Annual Mobility Workshop
 WHEN: Thursday, October 29, 2026 | 4:30 - 7:00 pm
WHERE: Gangal Hall, Engineering East, Florida Atlantic University, Boca Raton

COST: FREE
 REGISTRATION: Pre-registration required due to limited capacity.

EVENT SCHEDULE:

  • 4:30–5:30 p.m. | Exhibit Hall 
     Meet with local agencies and community partners. 
  • 5:30–6:00 p.m. | City Mobility Project Updates 
     The City’s Public Works & Engineering staff will provide updates on current mobility programs.
  • 6:00–7:00 p.m. | Student Poster Presentations 
     FAU students will share innovative ideas for the future of mobility.

The workshop reflects the City’s ongoing commitment to a safe, efficient and interconnected multimodal transportation system that serves residents and visitors today while planning for Boca Raton’s future.

For more information and to register, visit the City’s Mobility Workshop webpage.

News Flash

Boca Raton's Night Market Lights Up Sanborn Square This Fall

Media Releases Posted on September 28, 2026

Food, art, music & community spirit return downtown starting October 1, with a holiday-themed Night Market in December

When the sun sets over Sanborn Square this fall, downtown Boca Raton comes alive. The City's beloved Night Market series returns Thursday, October 1, 2026, from 6–9 p.m. (72 N Federal Hwy), kicking off a monthly evening of food, art, and music in the heart of downtown.

This season's dates are set for October, November, and December.

Each Night Market transforms Sanborn Square into an open-air festival featuring vendors offering traditional market fare like baked goods and sweet treats, alongside local artists and makers, with music filling the air throughout the evening.

Upcoming Night Market Dates

October 1, 2026

November 5, 2026

December 10, 2026

Attendees can take advantage of free rides to and from the Night Market with BocaConnect, the City's eco-friendly shuttle service. Simply download the Circuit App to request a ride in just a few clicks.

"Our Night Markets are one of the best ways to experience everything that makes Boca Raton special — great food, local art, music, and a real sense of community," said Mayor Andy Thomson. "We can't wait to welcome everyone back to Sanborn Square this season, especially for our holiday-themed market in December."

For more details on the Night Market, visit www.myboca.us.

About the City of Boca Raton: 

Boca Raton, the second largest city in Palm Beach County, blends history and innovation with its Mediterranean Revival architecture and vibrant cultural scene. Influenced by architect Addison Mizner, the city is home to live concerts, international art exhibits, world-class museums, five miles of Atlantic coastline, and 49 parks offering 1,650 acres of recreational space. A hub for business and innovation, Boca Raton hosts 40 publicly traded corporate headquarters. With three nationally ranked universities, top-rated schools, and a thriving entrepreneurial ecosystem, Boca Raton is a dynamic, safe, and educated community with a low property tax rate. Learn more at myboca.us.

News Flash

Boca Raton's Halloween Season is Here

Media Releases Posted on September 28, 2026

HOWL-O-WEEN AND BOO-CA BOO DAYS BRING THE FRIGHTS AND FUN

From a Costume Contest for Dogs to Weeks of Family-Friendly Halloween Programming, the City's October Lineup Has Something for Everyone

Boca Raton is going all in on Halloween this year, with a season of frights and fun for two- and four-legged residents alike. The City’s Recreation Services Department is rolling out Boo-ca Boo Days, a lineup of Halloween programming at parks, libraries and community centers throughout October, while dogs and their humans get their own celebration with Howl-O-Ween.

🐾 Howl-O-Ween

Forget trick-or-treating — this October, Boca Raton’s four-legged residents are stealing the Halloween spotlight. The City of Boca Raton is throwing, a free, tail-wagging morning of costumes, contests and canine chaos, on Saturday, October 24, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at Countess de Hoernle Park.

Dust off the dog costume and grab a leash — this is one Halloween party where the humans are just the plus-one.

Event Schedule:

  • 9:30 a.m. – Muttville Comix Dog Show: Local pups show off their best tricks — and their best comedic timing.
  • 10:30 a.m. – Howl-O-Weener Dog Race Contest: Short legs, big dreams. Boca's fastest wiener dogs take the track.
  • 11:30 a.m. – Howl-O-Ween Costume Contest: From pumpkins to pirates, the best-dressed dog in town takes home the crown.

More Events & Activities

When the pups aren't racing or strutting the runway, there's plenty more to sniff out:

  • Trail of Treats – a not-so-spooky trail loaded with pup-approved surprises
  • Photo Booth – because every good costume deserves its own paparazzi moment
  • Crafts – make a keepsake craft together, featuring your pup's own paw print
  • Paw Spa – free nail trims to keep those paws party-ready
  • Sit, Stay, Chill Lounge – a shady spot to rest up, with free teeth and ear cleanings available
  • Hydration Station – water breaks for the hardest-working tails in town
  • Community Partners – local organizations sharing pet resources and good vibes
  • Sponsor Giveaways – freebies, because no good goodie bag ever hurt anybody

The City is still looking for vendors for the Trail of Treats! Fill out the Trail of Treats Vendor Application Form to participate, or visit Howl-O-Ween | Boca Raton, FL for more information.

Boca Raton Is a Pet-Friendly City

It's no secret Boca Raton is a dog's kind of town. The city is proud to be certified as a Better Cities for Pets™ city, a recognition it earned in 2024 for its pet-friendly parks, programs and policies. Among its standout amenities are Mizner Bark Dog Park and Bark Beach at Spanish River Park, along with pet-friendly restaurants and housing throughout the city. Visit the Pets in Boca Raton webpage to learn more.

🎃 Boo-ca Boo Days

While the dogs get their day at Howl-O-Ween, the rest of the family can dive into Boo-ca Boo Days, the City’s month-long lineup of Halloween programming at libraries, parks and nature centers throughout October. 

Highlights include:

  • Silly Spooky Bubble Party (Sat, Oct 3, 9:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.) – Boca Raton Public Library, Spanish River. Music, dance, bubbles and glow-in-the-dark ball activities for all ages; costumes welcome. Free.
  • The Witch’s Lair: A Halloween Escape Room (Sat, Oct 10, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.) – Boca Raton Public Library, Spanish River. Ages 9–17 solve clues to break a witch’s curse and escape before time runs out. Free, registration required.
  • Ghostly Glows and Ghoulish Gases (Oct 17 & 18, 3:30 p.m.) – Children’s Science Explorium. A spooky science demonstration for ages 7+. Free.
  • Pumpkin Pals Make & Take (Sat, Oct 17, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.) – Sugar Sand Park Community Center. Ages 5–10 drop in to create three festive Halloween crafts. Resident $12, Non-resident $15.
  • Halloween by the Sea (Sun, Oct 18, 4:30–5:30 p.m. or 5:45–6:45 p.m.) – Gumbo Limbo Nature Center. Pre-school games, crafts, treats and a photo with Luna the sea turtle for ages 2–6. Resident $10, Non-resident $13.
  • Little Boos Storytime (Wed, Oct 21, 11 a.m.–1 p.m.) – Sugar Sand Park Community Center. A not-so-scary storytime, craft and snack for ages 18 months–4 years. Resident $5, Non-resident $6.25.
  • The History Behind: Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (Wed, Oct 21, 1–2:30 p.m.) – Boca Raton Public Library, Spanish River. A talk on the origins of the classic novel, for ages 18+. Free.
  • Monster Mash (Sun, Oct 25, 12–2 p.m.) – The Swim Center. Face painting, deck games and a pumpkin dive in the pool, for all ages. Free.
  • Spooky Tennis (Fri, Oct 30, 6 p.m.) – Racquet Center. A costumed round robin for ages 7–12. Resident $30, Non-resident $37.50.
  • Family Halloween Feature Film: Hocus Pocus (1993) (Fri, Oct 30, 6:30–8:30 p.m.) – Boca Raton Public Library, Spanish River. An outdoor screening on the library patio for the whole family. Free.
  • Creepy Crawlies at the Chickee Lab (Oct 30, 4:30–5:30 p.m. or 6–7 p.m.) – Children’s Science Explorium. Meet spooky animal ambassadors and make nature-inspired crafts, ages 5–12. Resident $10, Non-resident $12.50.
  • Night Explorers Nocturnal Hike (Fri, Oct 30, 7–8:30 p.m.) – Gumbo Limbo Nature Center. A guided nighttime hike to learn about nocturnal creatures, ages 7+. Resident $12, Non-resident $15.

That’s in addition to Howl-O-Ween on October 24, detailed above. For the full schedule, ages, costs and registration links for every Boo-ca Boo Days event, visit myboca.us/2813/Boca-Boo-Days-Events.

Howl-O-Ween Rules & Guidelines

Every good party needs a few ground rules. Here's what to know before you go:

  • All dogs must be on a leash at all times.
  • Please clean up after your dog. Bag stations and trash cans are available throughout the event space.
  • Aggressive behavior must be addressed immediately. In the event of aggression, please move your dog to another part of the park or leave the park.
  • Persons in violation of these rules may be required to leave the park.
  • Dog owners are responsible for, and liable with respect to, the actions of their dogs and any damage or injury to person or property caused by same.

How to Get Involved

Howl-O-Ween is free, with no RSVP required and no costume too extra — just show up ready to howl. For the full schedule, activity details and event updates, visit myboca.us/3016/Howl-O-Ween. For the complete Boo-ca Boo Days lineup and registration details, visit myboca.us/2813/Boca-Boo-Days-Events.

News Flash

City to Host Red, White & Boca: A Veterans Day Celebration

Media Releases Posted on September 28, 2026

Free Community Event Honors Local Veterans with Live Music, a Classic Car Show, and a Veterans Marketplace on November 11

The City of Boca Raton invites the community to Red, White & Boca: A Veterans Day Celebration, a free event honoring the men and women who have served in the U.S. armed forces. The celebration will take place Wednesday, November 11, 2026, from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m. at the Mizner Park Amphitheater, 590 Plaza Real.

Open to veterans, their families, and community members of all ages, Red, White & Boca brings the city together for an afternoon of live music, inspiring speeches, and a shared spirit of unity and patriotism in recognition of those who have served. All are welcome, and no registration is required.

Veterans Marketplace

Alongside the day's musical lineup, a Veterans Marketplace will showcase local service organizations and veteran-owned small businesses from throughout the community. Businesses and organizations interested in participating can apply through the city's online marketplace application at myboca.us.

Classic Car Show

The event's east lawn will host a classic car show featuring awards for Best of Show, Best Veteran-Owned, and more, with award presentations at 6:45 p.m. 

Live Music & Entertainment

The celebration will feature performances from The Coastman Chorus and Belladiva, capturing the spirit of celebration and unity that defines the event.

Event Schedule

4:00 PM — Event begins: Veterans Marketplace, Classic Car Show, and food vendors open

4:45 PM — Presentation of Colors & National Anthem

4:55 PM — Speeches

5:10 PM — Performance: The Coastman Chorus

5:25 PM — Speeches

5:40 PM — Announcements

5:45 PM — Performance: Belladiva

6:45 PM — Car Show Award Presentation

Boca Raton is recognized as a Purple Heart City, a designation honoring the sacrifices and service of military veterans who have received the Purple Heart for bravery and valor in the line of duty. The city joins a distinguished list of communities nationwide that formally recognize and support those who have been wounded or killed in service to their country.

Red, White & Boca is free and open to the public. For more information, including the Veterans Marketplace application, visit myboca.us/1467/Veterans-Day.

About the City of Boca Raton:

Boca Raton, the second-largest city in Palm Beach County, blends history and innovation through its Mediterranean Revival architecture — influenced by famed architect Addison Mizner — and a vibrant cultural scene featuring live concerts, international art exhibits and world-class museums. The city offers five miles of Atlantic coastline and 49 parks spanning 1,650 acres of recreational space. A hub for business and innovation, Boca Raton is home to more than 40 publicly traded corporate headquarters. With three nationally ranked universities, top-rated schools and a thriving entrepreneurial ecosystem, Boca Raton is a dynamic, safe and educated community. Learn more at myboca.us.

Mayor Andy Thomson to Host Community Town Hall

Media Releases Posted on September 25, 2026 | Last Updated on September 25, 2026

City of Boca Raton Mayor Andy Thomson will host a Town Hall meeting on Wednesday, October 14, offering residents an opportunity to hear directly from the Mayor about what’s happening in Boca Raton, upcoming City initiatives, and issues that matter to the community.

The Town Hall is designed to provide an informal setting for open dialogue between residents and the Mayor.
